generatedProse.concept-context: In psychology, self-regulated learning shows in how you approach a piece of empirical work. Rather than reading around a topic until a deadline forces a write-up, a self-regulating student sets a clear question, chooses which studies and methods to focus on, checks part-way whether the evidence is building towards an answer, and evaluates the finished argument against the standard. The discipline rewards that deliberate, monitored approach.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Two psychology students have four weeks to write the same essay on a contested theory.

Tom starts reading straight away and writes as the studies accumulate, with no goal beyond covering the theory and no check on whether the argument is building, until the essay comes back with a disappointing mark. Tom was busy throughout, but never stood back to monitor or adjust. This is working without regulating.

Amara begins by setting a goal: a clear position on the theory, supported by the strongest evidence, finished a week early. Amara chooses which studies to weigh, checks at the halfway point whether the argument holds, and drops a line of evidence that is not working. Afterwards Amara notes what to do differently next time. This is self-regulated learning: forethought, performance and evaluation, run on purpose.

Both students worked hard. Only Amara drove the process, and it is Amara who will improve from one essay to the next.
generatedProse.summary: Self-regulated learning in psychology means driving your own work through forethought, performance and evaluation: setting a question and strategy, monitoring whether the evidence is building, and judging the result against the standard. You can now explain the process and see it at work in a student's approach. The next lesson turns to one tool of self-regulation: judging your own work against the marking criteria.

check.body: In the worked example, what made Amara self-regulating rather than simply hard-working?

items.text: She set a goal, monitored whether her argument was building, and adjusted her evidence along the way.
She spent more hours on the essay than Tom did.
She started her reading earlier than Tom did.
She asked the tutor for more guidance before starting.

feedback.correct: That's right. Setting a goal, monitoring the argument and adjusting the evidence is self-regulation in action.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look for what Amara DID with the process, beyond working hard.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Amara was self-regulating because she set a goal, monitored whether her argument was building, and adjusted her evidence. Extra hours, an earlier start or more guidance are not the point.
